bull.t: Scalable IP licensing and royalty model
bull.b: Arm’s asset-light model monetizes the same processor architectures across many customers and end markets, while royalties can expand as customer chip shipments grow. The licensing base and software ecosystem also support repeat adoption, creating durable operating leverage and recurring revenue potential.

bull.t: Strong margins, cash generation and balance sheet
bull.b: Very high gross margins, substantial free cash flow and minimal leverage give Arm financial flexibility to fund research, ecosystem expansion and new products internally. Strong operating cash coverage also supports earnings quality and reduces the balance-sheet constraints that can limit strategic investment.

bull.t: Expanding AI and data-center platform position
bull.b: Rapid data-center royalty growth and stronger-than-expected AGI CPU demand indicate that Arm is extending beyond its established mobile base into higher-value AI infrastructure. Broader cloud and infrastructure adoption could diversify revenue and increase royalty opportunities as AI workloads scale.

bear.b: Smartphones remain an important royalty end market, so weaker handset economics can reduce chip volumes or delay customer purchasing decisions. Management’s lower royalty-growth expectations show that this exposure may temper consolidated growth even as data-center and AI demand expands.

bear.t: Supply constraints limit AGI CPU ramp
bear.b: Demand above the initial AGI CPU target may not translate into revenue quickly if Arm and its partners cannot secure enough wafers, substrates, testing and memory. Capacity bottlenecks can delay customer deployments, constrain near-term upside and extend the time needed to scale the product.

The AGI CPU launch broadens Arm’s opportunity but initially carries lower margins than its traditional IP economics, while development requires elevated investment. Until scale and product maturity improve profitability, the initiative could dilute margins and make earnings more sensitive to execution.
